basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 5.' and it opens '| Vers. 5. Sicut Ruben et Simeon reputabantur mihi. Id est, suas per se tribus facient,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 5. Sicut Ruben et Simeon reputabantur mihi. Id est, suas per se tribus facient, ut jam non dicatur tribus Joseph, sed tribus Ephraim et Manasse. Sicut Simeon et Ruben suas tribus singulas facient, sic Ephraim et Manasse duae tribus erunt, et sic tredecim tribus perficientur, Joseph tribu in duas partes divisa.
